answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to stake a scarce, time-locked deposit before it can trade, like planting a flag in a tundra that only one claimant can hold. New identities start with near-zero trust and must earn reputation through verified, useful work over time, so a flood of fresh accounts cannot outvote established ones. A comet of quick fake signups then burns out: creating many identities costs real capital, while honest agents keep their stake and their history, making saffron-priced fraud uneconomic compared with genuine participation.
